units.title: Pleural Anatomy and Fluid Composition, Detection Thresholds, and Light's Criteria with the Diuretic Disadvantage
units.sec: Pleural Anatomy and Fluid Composition, Detection Thresholds, and Light's Criteria with the Diuretic Disadvantage
units.guide:
The mesothelial-lined pleural cavity (p260) holds 10–20 ml of fluid at negative pressure from its lymphatics and vacuum, coupling lung to chest wall; parietal pleura from somatopleuric mesoderm is pain sensitive and visceral pleura from splanchnopleural mesoderm is pain insensitive ('Developes' as printed).
Effusions need 50 mL for USG or a lateral film, 200 mL for a PA film and 300 mL clinically; normal fluid is 70% macrophages, 25% lymphocytes and 1–5% mesothelial cells, with blood-level glucose, protein 1–1.5 g/dL and LDH under half of plasma.
Light's criteria separate exudate from transudate — protein ratio at least 0.5, LDH ratio at least 0.6, or pleural LDH above two-thirds of the serum upper limit, any one making an exudate — but misclassify a third of diuresed CCF effusions, where a higher serum–pleural albumin gradient instead indicates a transudate.

units.title: Transudative and Exudative Causes, Drugs Causing Effusion, TB Effusion Presentation and General Examination Signs
units.sec: Transudative and Exudative Causes, Drugs Causing Effusion, TB Effusion Presentation and General Examination Signs
units.guide:
Transudates (p261) number CCF with NT pro BNP in fluid, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome, hypothyroidism, hypoalbuminemia, Budd-Chiari syndrome, chronic constrictive pericarditis, SVC obstruction as printed, peritoneal dialysis and urinothorax with low pH, high creatinine and ammoniacal odor; exudates number TB, pneumonia, malignancy, RA/SLE connective tissue disease and the left-sided pair acute pancreatitis and esophageal rupture, with pulmonary infarction and embolism causing both types and nitrofurantoin, dantrolene, methysergide and bromocriptine as drug causes.
TB effusion strikes women of 20–30 years at first exposure, its pleuritic pain easing as fluid collects, and 25–30% develop pulmonary TB over 5–10 years.
Examination shows contralateral tracheal deviation (the film: left effusion deviating the trachea right), confirmed on palpation with reduced fremitus and movement, stony dull percussion, and reduced breath sounds and vocal resonance.

units.title: Parapneumonic Effusion and Empyema, Low-pH Causes, and Chylothorax versus Pseudochylothorax
units.sec: Parapneumonic Effusion and Empyema, Low-pH Causes, and Chylothorax versus Pseudochylothorax
units.guide:
Uncomplicated parapneumonic effusion (p262) is a sterile inflammatory leak with normal glucose, pH 7.3–7.4 and high protein/LDH, while bacterial invasion with fibrin and septation makes it complicated — glucose below 60 (printed g/L), pH below 7.2, very high LDH above 1000 and protein, Gram stain positive.
Empyema adds macroscopic pus, protein above 8 g/dL, LDH above 1000 IU/L and the CT split pleura sign against a pulmonary abscess; low fluid pH also marks rheumatoid arthritis and malignancy, the latter with poor prognosis.
Milky fluid splits into chylothorax of lymphatic rupture from trauma or lymphoma, rich in triglyceride, and pseudochylothorax of pleural thickening in TB or RA, an exudate enriched with cholesterol crystals above 250 mg/dL.

units.title: Pleural Fluid Glucose, ICD Indications, Eosinophils in Pleural Fluid, and Tuberculous and Neoplastic Effusion Diagnosis
units.sec: Pleural Fluid Glucose, ICD Indications, Eosinophils in Pleural Fluid, and Tuberculous and Neoplastic Effusion Diagnosis
units.guide:
Fluid glucose (p263) falls below 60 mg/dL in RA, empyema, malignancy and SLE (under 20% as printed) and below 30 mg/dL in RA, while NT pro BNP in fluid means a cardiac cause.
An intercostal drain is indicated for 'calculated effusion' as printed, pH below 7.2, glucose below 60 mg/dL or pus; fluid eosinophils suggest lung fluke, asbestosis, histoplasmosis, lung infarction, effusion-causing drugs or hemo/pneumothorax, and the loculated right effusion film keeps its trachea central.
Tuberculous effusion is best proven by biopsy plus culture at 90% sensitivity over fluid CBNAAT 45–50%, culture 25–50% and stain 10–20%; neoplastic effusion is headed by mesothelioma as printed and breast metastasis, needs VAT (as printed) or CT-guided biopsy beyond 50%-sensitive cytology, and carries a poor prognosis except in lymphoma.
